title: Projection formula for an immersion extension by zero
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be an immersion with a chosen factorization $S\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, where $i$ is closed and $j$ is open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $Rs_!=j_!i_*$, $Rs^!=Ri^!j^*$ and let $Rs_*$ denote ordinary derived direct image; $j_!$ is exact extension by zero [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], and $Ri^!$ is the ambient right adjoint of $i_*$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and derived internal Hom $\mathscr H_T(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the canonical projection map
$$\pi_{s,C,P}:C\otimes_A^LRs_!P\longrightarrow Rs_!(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)$$
is an isomorphism natural in both inputs. For a cartesian pullback square with $s':S'\hookrightarrow X'$ and projections $g_X,g_S$, under the canonical tensor identifications and the canonical extension-by-zero base-change isomorphism $b_P:g_X^*Rs_!P\cong Rs'_!g_S^*P$, composed of the open extension-by-zero base change and the finite (closed-immersion) exchange isomorphism $g_U^*i_*\cong i'_*g_S^*$ [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], $g_X^*\pi_{s,C,P}$ is $\pi_{s',g_X^*C,g_S^*P}$.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); agent derived immersion projection formula and cartesian compatibility, with closed-support detection as in etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle).

proof.text: Because a closed immersion is finite, its direct image is exact; the open extension-by-zero and all constant-coefficient inverse images in the statement are exact as well. Choose K-flat resolutions with flat terms for the complexes $C$ and $P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Exact inverse image preserves these resolutions and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] computes all derived tensors by their total tensor complexes and supplies the canonical pullback-tensor comparisons. Thus the desired comparison can be checked on flat-term representatives, and all subsequent sheaf maps descend canonically to the unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Tags 01WN/03S2, 0E8I; exactness and K-flat reduction used in the proof

proof.text: For a flat-term complex $P$ and a term of $C$, the canonical sheaf map $(j^*C)\otimes_A i_*P\to i_*(i^*j^*C\otimes_A P)$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk. Indeed a finite closed fibre is empty or a singleton, so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] identify the target stalk with the tensor of the two corresponding stalks; the inverse-image germ isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies $(i^*j^*C)_{\bar z}$ with $(j^*C)_{i\bar z}$, and [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] identifies this tensor with the stalk of the source. [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] then gives the sheaf isomorphism. Applying this degreewise and totalizing, with the K-flat computation of Step 1, yields the natural derived isomorphism $j^*C\otimes_A^L i_*P\cong i_*(i^*j^*C\otimes_A^L P)$.

source.place: Tag 0A45, support-stalk calculation, combined with sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] to the open immersion $j$ with $E=i_*P$ and $N=C$, and use the symmetry of the derived tensor. Its target is $j_!(i_*P\otimes_A^Lj^*C)$. Substitute the closed isomorphism of Step 2 and the canonical composition/monoidal identifications [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal, lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] to identify this target with $j_!i_*(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)=Rs_!(s^*C\otimes_A^LP)$. The resulting composite is exactly the canonical projection map $\pi_{s,C,P}$. Every comparison used is natural, so this proves that $\pi_{s,C,P}$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; composition identifications from the derived pullback conventions

proof.text: For a Cartesian pullback, the closed square is again a closed immersion. At each geometric point of $U'$ the finite fibre is empty or a singleton, and the finite exchange isomorphism $g_U^*i_*\cong i'_*g_S^*$, compatible with the stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], the closed-pushforward stalk identification [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar], and the inverse-image germ isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] carry the Step 2 closed tensor map to the corresponding primed map. The inverse-image monoidal comparison and the pullback-composition equation [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal, lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] identify all tensor and restriction associators. Therefore the closed isomorphism of Step 2 is compatible with pullback; geometric-stalk conservativity proves equality of the canonical maps globally.

source.place: Tags 03S6 and 0A45; stalk and germ compatibility in the Cartesian square

proof.text: Use the open projection/base-change identity [lem-asd-open-projection-exchange] with $a=g_X$, $E=i_*P$, and $N=C$. Its $d$-map is precisely the canonical comparison from the pulled-back closed tensor object to the closed tensor object on $S'$ by Step 4. The base-change map for the open extension is the inverse of the module mate by [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility], hence agrees with the specified $b_P$ under the canonical identifications. Compose the identity with the closed compatibility of Step 4 and the monoidal and composition comparisons [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal, lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal]. The resulting equality is exactly $g_X^*\pi_{s,C,P}=\pi_{s',g_X^*C,g_S^*P}$ under the tensor and $b_P$ identifications.

The statement is true and keeps the item's setting: A is a finite commutative ring, the category is ordinary unbounded D(T_et,A), and Rs_!=j_!i_*. No hypothesis is added. Edge cases checked: S empty, i=id (0GL1), j=id (closed stalk computation), s=id, and base change with S' empty. Steps 1, 3 and 5 are correct. Step 1: K-flat C makes j^*C and i^*j^*C K-flat, so the derived tensors are total tensors. Step 3 uses lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor with K=i_*P. Step 5 uses lem-asd-open-projection-exchange with a=g_X, and lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility identifies its open base-change map with the open factor of b_P. I repaired three missing citations: (1) Step 2 identifies the stalk of i^*j^*C without citing lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ; added. (2) Step 4 uses the closed-pushforward stalk identification without citing lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar; added. (3) Step 4 and the statement's b_P need the global closed exchange isomorphism g_U^*i_* ≅ i'_*g_S^*, and stalkwise matching does not give a sheaf map. The existing lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange states it: it is on the route (sk-thm-p1), closed in slopmaster2, and creates no cycle. I added it to stmt_deps and Step 4 and named it as a factor of b_P. The statement's content is unchanged. Batch-5 check: lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar (sec-poincare-duality) is genuinely outside both assumed statements. It is the generic fact that the stalk of a tensor is the tensor of the stalks, with scalar extension (Stacks 008B/007K). It was created for the lisse tensor infrastructure and is not a step of the Poincare duality or trace formula proofs. Its 65-node closure contains no other sec-poincare-duality or sec-trace-formula node, and many non-PD nodes already cite it, including the parent thm-weil-etale-geometric-biduality. I kept it. Accepted tool uses: lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor and lem-asd-open-projection-exchange (both declared), plus the generic cbc, kun, recollement and stalk nodes.
